title: WEF Energy Transition Index 2026
text:
The World Economic Forum (WEF) released its Energy Transition Index 2026 on 18 June 2026. The index is produced by the WEF in collaboration with Accenture and covers 120 countries. It benchmarks national energy systems across three core dimensions, security, sustainability and equity, and also measures the readiness of the enabling environment that supports the transition.

Sweden, Finland and Denmark retained the top three positions in the 2026 ranking. India ranked 70th, moving up two places, and its overall score improved by 1.9 per cent over the year. The WEF described India as one of the strongest improvers globally, citing a sharp rise in infrastructure and broad-based gains across the system.

According to the report, the main drivers of India's improved performance were the achievement of universal access to electricity, the replacement of solid fuels with clean cooking options, and an increase in renewable energy deployment. Renewable energy employment in India reached 1.3 million jobs in 2024, up 25 per cent over 2023, with hydropower the largest source of such jobs. The share of low-carbon jobs in the country rose by 24 per cent in the same year.

Singapore was among the biggest climbers, rising 10 places to 42nd. Among G20 members, Germany placed ninth, France tenth, the United Kingdom eleventh, China fourteenth, Brazil seventeenth and the United States nineteenth.

The global findings were less encouraging. Total global energy investment reached a record 3.3 trillion US dollars, including 2.3 trillion dollars in clean energy. Energy security deteriorated, and transition readiness declined for the first time in more than a decade. The WEF said a growing gap between capital deployment and transition readiness meant that investment alone no longer sustained momentum.

notes.questions_not_written: No questions written. The WebSearch budget was exhausted (200 per turn) before the static-GK facts could be sourced. Every answer needs a non-passage fact with a source URL, and none were confirmed.
notes.conflicting_source: Outlook Business, dtnext and similar outlets report India at 67th. Those articles refer to the 2023 edition. The 2026 rank of 70th is used.
notes.unverified_single_source: Energy-mix caveat, green hydrogen focus, Strait of Hormuz remarks, and the 'only major economy' phrasing were found in one source each and were left out.
